issues.legal_issue: A deposit for payment to the decree-holder is unnecessary on an application to set aside an execution sale when the decree has already been satisfied or adjusted.
material_facts: A receiver applied to set aside an execution sale and did not deposit the amount specified for payment to the decree-holder.
The decree had not been satisfied or adjusted when the application was made; the Court stated that satisfaction or adjustment would remove the need for the deposit.
issues.conclusion: If the decree has been satisfied or adjusted by the time the application is made, a deposit for payment to the decree-holder is not required.
issues.legal_principle: Under Order XXI, rule 89(b) of the Code of Civil Procedure, the required deposit for payment to the decree-holder is unnecessary if the decree has already been satisfied or adjusted. An adjustment may be recorded under Order XXI, rule 2.

predicates.sale_setting_application: A judgment debtor or a representative applies to set aside an execution sale.
predicates.decree_satisfied: The judgment debtor has discharged the decree before making the application.
predicates.decree_adjusted: The parties have adjusted the decree before making the application.

issues.definition: When an application to set aside an execution sale is made after the decree has been discharged or adjusted, no deposit for the decree-holder is required.

issues.legal_issue: A decree-holder’s agreement to postpone collection while provision for future payment is pursued does not dispense with the required deposit when the decree remains unsatisfied and unadjusted.
material_facts: A receiver applied to set aside a sale of trust property and deposited the amounts payable to the purchaser but not the amount specified for the decree-holder.
The decree-holder agreed to postpone realizing the decree while provision for payment was pursued in a separate suit, but the decree remained alive and had not been satisfied or adjusted.
The receiver asked the court to dispense with the deposit, and the lower court granted that request; the High Court set that order aside.
issues.conclusion: The agreement to postpone collection did not obviate the deposit requirement, so the deposit for the decree-holder remained necessary and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Order XXI, rule 89(b) of the Code of Civil Procedure requires the deposit for payment to the decree-holder unless the decree has been satisfied or adjusted. A promise to take steps toward future payment, or an agreement merely to postpone realization, does not itself satisfy or adjust the decree; an adjustment capable of being recorded is contemplated by Order XXI, rule 2. The Court discussed Union of India v. Kishorilal Gupta and Bros. on discharge of a contract by mutual agreement, but held that the facts did not show an agreement by the decree-holder to forego rights under the decree.

rule.if: sale_setting_application and creditor_only_postponed_collection and future_payment_provision_pursued and decree_remains_unsatisfied_and_unadjusted

predicates.sale_setting_application: A judgment debtor or a representative applies to set aside an execution sale.
predicates.creditor_only_postponed_collection: The decree-holder agreed only to delay collection of the decree debt, rather than give up the rights under the decree.
predicates.future_payment_provision_pursued: The parties pursued a provision for payment to be made in the future.
predicates.decree_remains_unsatisfied_and_unadjuste: The decree remained undischarged and unadjusted when the application was made.

issues.definition: When an application to set aside an execution sale is made, a mere postponement of collection while future payment provision is pursued does not remove the deposit requirement if the decree remains undischarged and unadjusted.
